evidence.claim: Top Features to Look for in Modern Note-Taking Apps - DEV Community
evidence.evidence:
6. Collaboration Features
Modern note-taking apps are often used in collaborative settings, making features like sharing, commenting, and editing crucial for teams. Apps such as Google Keep and Notion allow multiple users to edit, view, or comment on notes simultaneously, fostering teamwork and productivity. Real-time collaboration is beneficial in both professional and academic settings, as it enables seamless information sharing and easy project management.
7. Integration with Other Apps [...] 10. Security and Privacy
With the sensitive information we often store in note-taking apps, security is paramount. Features like password protection, end-to-end encryption, and two-factor authentication are essential to protect your data. Apps like Standard Notes and Zoho Notebook are known for their strong encryption policies, ensuring that only you have access to your notes. Before choosing an app, review its privacy policy to understand how your data is stored and secured.
11. Multimedia Support [...] 9. Offline Access
Sometimes, you need access to your notes even when you're offline. Whether you’re traveling, in a meeting without Wi-Fi, or simply prefer to work without distractions, offline access is crucial. Many apps, such as OneNote and Notion (paid version), offer offline functionality, allowing you to view and edit your notes without an internet connection. When you reconnect, changes are automatically synced.

evidence.claim: The 7 best note taking apps in 2026
evidence.evidence:
Second, all the note-taking apps had to be quick and easy to use as intended. The real competition when you're looking for somewhere to write a note isn't other note-taking apps, but a pen and scrap of paper. If it wasn't almost as convenient to open the notes app and create a quick note as it was to reach across my desk for an index card and a pen, it didn't make the cut. This rule also extended to other features: editing and sorting notes had to feel seamless and natural, rather than require a battle with a horrible user interface. [...] The closest direct competitor to Evernote on this list
 Free and open source (though syncing through Joplin Cloud is extra)
Joplin cons:
 Less polished than the competition
Not only is Joplin the best open source note-taking app on this list, but it's also the best free Evernote alternative too. For a number of reasons I'll explore below, Evernote is a lot harder to recommend than it was a decade ago despite some recent improvements. But because Evernote has been such a staple of the note-taking app space, many other apps have gone different directions in order to compete. OneNote is awesome, but using it is a totally different experience to using Evernote. Joplin, though, gets things pretty close—and you can import all your notebooks from Evernote. [...] One thing to note: Notion bills itself as an Evernote competitor for personal users. It can be—but it's too much for most people. If you love the idea of Notion, go right ahead and try the free Personal Plan, but for me, it's really best as a team notes app or an AI-powered notes app. Apps like Obsidian (which I'll get to in a moment) and Craft have a lot of Notion's best features, but they're tailored for individuals.
